To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the N-terminal tail of Hec1 is sufficient to bind to microtubule tails in vitro, and that this interaction is essential for kinetochores to attach and move chromosomes.
the N-terminal tail of the Ndc-80 complex subunit Hec1 is required for kinetochore microtubule attachment.
the unstructured N-terminal tails of Hec1 are necessary and sufficient to mediate kinetochore attachments to dynamic microtubules.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which cells ensure the accurate distribution of chromosomes during cell division.
how cells attach microtubules to chromosomes, and how this attachment is regulated.
the molecular basis of chromosome movements during mitosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
kinetochore microtubule attachment is mediated through a direct ionic interaction between the N-terminal tail of the Hec1 subunits of the outer kinetochore and the microtubule minus ends.
the N-terminal tail of Hec1 is required for kinetochore attachment to microtubule plus ends, and this interaction is mediated primarily by ionic interactions.
the N-terminal tail of the Ndc 80(Hec1 ) subunit (H ec1) is necessary for kinetochore microtubule attachment and that this tail binds microtubules via ionic interactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the N-terminal tail of Hec1 binds to the negatively charged tail of the microtubule and that this is the main interaction that is required for the attachment and movement of the kinetochores.
kinetochore attachments to dynamic microtubule plus ends require an ionic interaction between unstructured domains.
the kinetochoretubule interface requires a direct interaction between the positively charged N-terminal tail of Hec1 and the negatively charged C-terminal tails of the tubulin dimer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
kinetochores attach to microtubule tails, not the plus end.
the Ndc80(Hect1) subunit of the Ndc10 complex is required for chromosome congression, spindle elongation, and cold-stable microtubule attachments to kinetochores.
the N-terminal tails on the microtubule and Hec1 are sufficient for high-affinity binding.
